title: The Menu Step Function
prompt: Write handle(tasks, choice, arg) — one iteration of a task-manager menu: 'add' -> add arg (default 'untitled'), 'done' -> complete index int(arg) (invalid int or range: unchanged), 'clear' -> remove all done tasks, anything else -> unchanged. handle NEVER prints. Returns the (possibly new) list.

tests.name: one menu iteration
tests.code:
t0 = [{"text": "a", "done": False}]
t1 = handle(t0, "add", "email")
assert t1[-1] == {"text": "email", "done": False}, f"add: {t1}"
assert handle(t0, "add")[-1]["text"] == "untitled", "missing arg -> untitled"
t2 = handle(t1, "done", "0")
assert t2[0]["done"] is True, f"done: {t2}"
assert handle(t1, "done", "99") == t1, "bad index -> unchanged"
assert handle(t1, "done", "x") == t1, "bad int -> unchanged"
t3 = handle(t2, "clear", "")
assert t3 == [{"text": "email", "done": False}], f"clear removes done only: {t3}"
assert handle(t0, "nonsense", "") == t0, "unknown choice -> unchanged"
tests.hint: int(arg) in try/except ValueError; reuse complete-style logic; 'clear' filters not t['done'].
